newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft on U.S. long bond yield.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft on U.S. long bond yield.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early gains against the dollar to close slightly weaker under pressure from the U.S. bond market and sagging share prices on the Mexican bourse, traders said.
"Many dealers speculated this morning on the peso gaining further ground...but started buying dollars again when they saw the U.S. long bond weaken," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.5 and 0.3 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.9000/7.9040 and 7.8960/7.8790 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.9 centavos firmer at 7.8750/7.8790 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was down 13/32 to yield 7.10 percent in late trade, while the Mexican bourse was down 0.64 percent to 3,768.57 when the foreign exchange market closed.
Traders said expected increases in domestic interest rates did not prevent late weakness in the peso.
"Increased interest rates may suit investors, but they make forex dealers nervous," another trader said.

Money market dealers surveyed by Reuters forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 22.66 percent at its weekly auction to be held later in the day. This would be a rise of 80 basis points since last week.
Auction results are due at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
